To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

large lipophilics drugs are prevented from entering brain due to their interactions with efflux transporters and that combining a large lipophilic drug with a smaller one can facilitate the brain entry of both drugs.
large lipophilics drugs such as proteases inhibitors have strong binding affinites to efflux transporters and are therefore prevented from entering the CNS.

large lipophillic drugs have strong binding affintities to efflux transporters and thus are prevented to enter the brain, but when combined, the one with the highest affinity will occupy a large portion of the efflux transporter binding sites and slow down the effux of the coadminstered PI thereby facilitating its entry in the brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physicochemical properties of ARVs that limit their brain entry.
the brain entry of ARV and the interactions between ARV and BBB transporters.
the development of new antiviral drugs for treatment of HIV-associated neurocognitve disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the brain entry of HIV drugs is a complex process that depends on the physicochemical characteristics of the drug, its affinity to BBB transporters, and interactions with other drugs.

the brain entry of HIV therapies combining small lipophilic drugs (e.g., nucleoside analogs) with large lipophilics (e.g., PI) is facilitated when used together, as the small lipophilic molecules can cross the BBB and then facilitate the brain entry of the large lipophilic ones.
the brain entry of ARV is facilitated when used as a combination and that the physicochemical characteristics of ARV are the major determinants of their brain entry.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of a boosting ritonavir in combination with a large lipophilic drug such as a PI would facilitate its brain entry.
the brain entry of ARV is facilitated by their combination, and the degree of facilitation depends on the physicochemical properties and the binding affinities of each ARV to drug transporters.
the brain entry of ARV is facilitated by the combined effect of their physicochemical properties and the interactions with the BBB transporters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HIV therapies combining large lipophilic PI with small diffusing molecules are better suited to cross the BBB and should be preferred in HIV-associated neurocognition disorders.
HIV-1 proteases inhibitors can be considered as "transporter blockers" and thus facilitate brain entry of other ARV.
the brain entry of ARV is not a simple function of lipophilicity but also of their physicochemical properties, which should be considered when developing new ARV.
